title: United States Loses Official Measles-Free Status
subtitle: Health authorities confirm the return of a disease that was once eliminated in the country.

summary.en: The United States has officially lost its measles-free status after outbreaks lasted longer than one year. Health experts describe this as a major setback for public health. Thousands of people have been sickened, and several deaths have been reported. Officials are debating the causes, including lower vaccination rates and government policy changes. Experts warn that the disease is entirely preventable with proper immunization.
summary.zh: 美國因麻疹疫情持續超過一年，已正式失去「麻疹根除國」的地位。衛生專家將此視為公共衛生的一大挫敗。目前已有數千人染病，並傳出多起死亡案例。官員們正針對疫情成因進行辯論，其中包括疫苗接種率下降與政府政策變更等因素。專家警告，透過適當的免疫接種，此疾病是完全可以預防的。

paragraphs.en: The United States has officially lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated. This announcement, confirmed by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), marks a major change for the nation. For twenty-five years, the U.S. had successfully kept the virus from spreading regularly within its borders. According to public health rules, a country loses this status if outbreaks continue for more than one year. That is exactly what has happened across the country.
paragraphs.zh: 美國已正式失去「麻疹根除國」的地位。這項由泛美衛生組織 (PAHO) 確認的公告，象徵該國出現了重大轉變。過去二十五年來，美國成功地將這種病毒阻絕於國境之內，使其無法持續傳播。根據公共衛生準則，若疫情持續超過一年，該國即會喪失此項地位，而這正是目前全美各地所發生的情況。

paragraphs.en: Anne Schuchat, an epidemiologist and former deputy director at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), described the news as a very sad moment. She explained that measles causes unnecessary suffering, including high fevers, long-term nerve damage, and even death. The disease is highly contagious, but it is also entirely preventable. Two doses of the measles-mumps-rubella vaccine can prevent about 97% of infections. When almost everyone in a community is vaccinated, the virus cannot spread.
paragraphs.zh: 流行病學家兼疾病管制與預防中心 (CDC) 前副主任舒查特 (Anne Schuchat) 將此消息形容為令人極度悲傷的時刻。她解釋說，麻疹會造成不必要的痛苦，包括高燒、長期神經損傷，甚至死亡。這種疾病傳染力極強，但卻完全可以預防。接種兩劑麻疹、腮腺炎、德國麻疹混合疫苗，能預防約百分之九十七的感染。當社區中幾乎每個人都接種疫苗時，病毒便無法傳播。

paragraphs.en: The human cost of this situation is significant. Researchers at Johns Hopkins University estimate that recent outbreaks have cost roughly $125 million in medical care and lost productivity. Over the past two years, more than 830 people have been hospitalized, and over 8,000 people have become sick. Tragically, states have reported 13 measles-associated deaths, including young infants in New York, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin. Babies are particularly at risk because they are usually too young to receive the vaccine.
paragraphs.zh: 此情況所造成的人力成本相當可觀。約翰霍普金斯大學 (Johns Hopkins University) 的研究人員估計，近期的疫情已造成約一億兩千五百萬美元的醫療照護支出與生產力損失。過去兩年來，已有超過八百三十人住院，逾八千人染病。令人遺憾的是，各州已通報十三起與麻疹相關的死亡案例，其中包括紐約州、賓夕法尼亞州與威斯康辛州的幼兒。嬰兒因年紀太小通常無法接種疫苗，因此面臨的風險特別高。

paragraphs.en: There is a strong disagreement regarding why this is happening. Emily Hilliard, a spokesperson for the Department of Health and Human Services, stated that the resurgence of the disease is due to vaccination gaps that began years ago. She noted that childhood vaccination rates have steadily dropped since the COVID-19 pandemic started. However, many scientists point to the current administration’s policies. They argue that the government has spread misinformation about vaccines and failed to respond quickly to outbreaks. For example, the administration cut millions of dollars from immunization programs and stopped funding research into why some people are hesitant to get vaccinated.
paragraphs.zh: 對於為何會發生這種情況，各界存在強烈分歧。衛生與公共服務部發言人希利亞德 (Emily Hilliard) 表示，疾病復燃是因為多年前就已出現的疫苗接種缺口。她指出，自新冠肺炎疫情爆發以來，兒童疫苗接種率便持續下降。然而，許多科學家將矛頭指向現任政府的政策。他們主張政府散布關於疫苗的錯誤資訊，且未能迅速應對疫情。例如，政府削減了數百萬美元的免疫計畫經費，並停止資助關於民眾為何對接種疫苗感到猶豫的研究。

paragraphs.en: Political tension has also risen within the health agencies. Susan Monarez, the former director of the CDC, was fired in August 2025. She told Congress that she was removed from her position because she refused to approve changes to vaccine recommendations without first reviewing the scientific evidence. Monarez warned that if vaccine protections are weakened, preventable diseases will continue to return. She noted that the country has already seen the largest measles outbreak in over 30 years.
paragraphs.zh: 衛生機構內部的政治緊張局勢也隨之升高。疾病管制與預防中心前主任莫納雷茲 (Susan Monarez) 於二零二五年八月遭到解職。她向國會表示，自己被撤職是因為她拒絕在未審閱科學證據的情況下，批准對疫苗建議事項的更動。莫納雷茲警告，若疫苗保護力被削弱，可預防的疾病將會持續回歸。她指出，美國已見證了三十多年來最嚴重的麻疹疫情。

paragraphs.en: In response to these criticisms, the White House and the Department of Health and Human Services have defended their actions. White House spokesperson Allison Schuster said that the President and the Health Secretary have encouraged people to get vaccinated. She added that the government has worked to coordinate with states and help move vaccine doses to areas where they are needed. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who led an anti-vaccine organization before taking his current role, remains at the center of this debate.
paragraphs.zh: 針對這些批評，白宮與衛生與公共服務部為其作為辯護。白宮發言人舒斯特 (Allison Schuster) 表示，總統與衛生部長一直鼓勵民眾接種疫苗。她補充說，政府已致力於與各州協調，協助將疫苗運送至有需求的地區。現任衛生部長小羅伯特·甘迺迪 (Robert F. Kennedy Jr.) 在接任現職前曾領導一個反疫苗組織，他目前仍是這場爭論的核心人物。

paragraphs.en: Public health experts are now looking at what comes next. The loss of measles-free status is a serious warning that the systems meant to protect the public are under pressure. As the virus continues to spread, the focus remains on closing the gap in vaccination rates. Without a major change in how the country handles immunizations, doctors fear that more preventable illnesses will return. For now, the focus is on preventing further deaths and ensuring that families understand the importance of the two-dose vaccine.
paragraphs.zh: 公共衛生專家現正關注接下來的發展。失去麻疹根除國地位是一個嚴重的警訊，顯示旨在保護大眾的系統正承受壓力。隨著病毒持續擴散，焦點仍放在彌補疫苗接種率的缺口上。若國家處理免疫接種的方式沒有重大改變，醫師們擔心更多可預防的疾病將會捲土重來。目前，重點在於防止更多死亡案例，並確保家庭了解兩劑疫苗的重要性。

keyTerms.definitionEn: The official position or condition of a country regarding a specific health classification.
keyTerms.noteZh: 此處指國家在國際衛生組織認證下的「狀態」，而非一般人理解的社會地位。文中：The United States has officially lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A difference or lack of something, in this case, a lack of sufficient vaccination coverage.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡指疫苗接種率不足的「缺口」，而非實體的縫隙。文中：She explained that the resurgence of the disease is due to vaccination gaps that began years ago.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Experiencing stress or being in a difficult situation that makes it hard to function properly.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 處於壓力之下、負擔沉重。
keyTerms.noteZh: 形容系統因負擔過重而運作困難。文中：The loss of measles-free status is a serious warning that the systems meant to protect the public are under pressure.

Meanwhile, debates continue regarding the government's approach to vaccine safety and public health policies.

quiz.question: According to the article, what is the specific condition that causes a country to lose its measles-eliminated status?

options.A: A failure to reach a 97% vaccination rate among the total population.
options.B: The occurrence of measles outbreaks that persist for more than one year.
options.C: A significant increase in the number of hospitalized infants across multiple states.
options.D: The government's decision to reduce funding for immunization research programs.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第一段明確指出：「According to public health rules, a country loses this status if outbreaks continue for more than one year.」選項 A 雖提到了 97% 的疫苗效力，但非失去狀態的定義；選項 C 是疫情的後果而非定義標準；選項 D 則是導致疫情的原因之一，而非失去狀態的技術性門檻。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the relationship between the current administration and public health experts?

options.A: They are in complete agreement regarding the necessity of mandatory vaccination policies.
options.B: The administration fully supports the CDC's historical recommendations without interference.
options.C: There is significant friction between scientific officials and political leadership over vaccine policy.
options.D: Public health experts have successfully convinced the White House to increase funding for research.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第四、五段，科學家批評政府散播不實資訊並刪減預算，且前 CDC 主任 Susan Monarez 因拒絕在缺乏科學證據下修改建議而被解職，顯示科學界與政府間存在嚴重衝突。選項 A 與事實相反；選項 B 被 Monarez 的案例反駁；選項 D 文章並未提及專家成功說服政府，反而是政府持續刪減預算。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the word 'pressure' mean in the context of 'the systems meant to protect the public are under pressure'?

options.A: A state of physical weight or force applied to an object.
options.B: The emotional feeling of stress or anxiety experienced by individuals.
options.C: A condition of being strained or burdened by excessive demands.
options.D: The act of forcing someone to do something against their will.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。在此語境中，「under pressure」指公共衛生系統因疫情爆發及政策變動，面臨極大的負擔與挑戰，處於一種不堪負荷的狀態。選項 A 是物理層面的壓力，不適用於系統；選項 B 指個人的心理壓力；選項 D 則是強迫他人，與句意不符。

quiz.question: Which of the following best summarizes the central message of the article?

options.A: The U.S. government has successfully coordinated with states to eliminate measles.
options.B: Measles is a minor illness that only affects infants who are too young for vaccines.
options.C: The loss of measles-free status highlights a critical failure in public health systems and policy.
options.D: The primary cause of the measles resurgence is the lack of medical care for hospitalized patients.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。本文核心在於探討美國失去麻疹消除國地位的嚴重性，並從疫情數據、政府政策爭議及專家觀點，分析公共衛生體系面臨的系統性困境。選項 A 與事實不符；選項 B 忽略了麻疹對所有人的威脅；選項 D 將重點放在醫療照護，而非疫情復燃的根本原因。
